selected_evidence.summary: Showed accept_redirects=1 (all/default) and secure_redirects=1 (all/default) before the fix; accept_source_route was already 0.
Created /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf and applied via sysctl --system; output shows all/default/eth0/lo accept_redirects, secure_redirects, accept_source_route all set to 0.

selected_evidence.requirement: Runtime effective values confirmed 0 including per-interface eth0
selected_evidence.summary: Initial check found eth0 still inheriting accept_redirects=1/secure_redirects=1 despite all/default=0; corrected by adding explicit eth0/lo entries, then reapplied and confirmed all values 0.

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + hardening state)
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 717db5a2-895d-4bfb-b8a8-d4891c7b7b01 and confirmed all hardening sysctls at 0 immediately before reboot.
systemctl reboot scheduled via backgrounded nohup command; tool call returned 'reboot_scheduled' before the node disconnected.

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof of actual restart (changed boot identity)
selected_evidence.summary: Connection reset confirmed the reboot took effect; subsequent poll returned new boot_id e9552362-9785-4beb-b609-00e9965f8377, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a real restart occurred.

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery and persistence of hardening
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, uptime showed a fresh boot time and all net.ipv4.conf.{all,default,eth0,lo}.{accept_redirects,secure_redirects,accept_source_route} sysctls remained 0; sysctl.d config file confirmed intact on disk.
